body.statement: For fixed rational \((p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) with interior observed cells and finite budgets, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) terminates and returns exact real-algebraic representations, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates for \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  Its candidate list is exhaustive over both exposure-odds boundary arcs and their endpoints, every legal analytic outcome-sign branch, and all interior stationary points.  It neither admits a cleared-denominator artifact nor omits a legal root, and it handles separately \(\Gamma_A=1\), \(\Gamma_a=1\), constant-\(U\) corners, root collisions, and positive-dimensional stationary continua.  This fixed-input output is not a symbolic atlas over varying observed summaries or budgets.
body.justification: An exact bound is operational only if every branch and degeneracy has a terminating, auditable certificate.
body.gap: Existing binary-\(U\) analyses use user-selected grids, and modern marginal-sensitivity bounds use convex duality; neither supplies a complete verifier for this algebraic common-law program.
body.consumer: A reproducible implementation can attach exact isolating intervals and branch witnesses to reported sensitivity endpoints.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a stratum and suppress \(x\).  All input numbers are rational, all budgets are finite, and \(p,r_0,r_1\in(0,1)\).  For each \(a\) and each legal endpoint \(\vartheta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}\), introduce a variable \(z_a\) and the polynomial
\[
F_a(w_a,z_a;\vartheta)
=(1-w_a)(\vartheta-1)z_a^2+\bigl[1+(w_a-r_a)(\vartheta-1)\bigr]z_a-r_a.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) proves that the additional inequalities
\[
0<z_a<1,
\qquad
1+(\vartheta-1)z_a>0
\]
select exactly one root of \(F_a=0\).  Therefore adjoining \(z_a\) is an exact semialgebraic graph construction, not a relaxation.  On that graph, \(m_{a,1}=\vartheta z_a/\{1+(\vartheta-1)z_a\}\) and every objective is rational with a denominator whose sign is known to be positive.

By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\), the signs of \(\pi-w_a\) choose the analytic endpoint formula for each \(q_a^-\) and \(q_a^+\).  The algorithm partitions \(D_A\) by the two affine sign polynomials \(\pi-w_a\), retains the equality faces as separate strata, and treats \(\Gamma_a=1\) by identifying the coincident endpoint branches.  Thus there are finitely many legal analytic branches.

For \(\Gamma_A>1\), the non-corner boundary of \(D_A\) consists of the two algebraic arcs
\[
w_1(1-w_0)=\Gamma_Aw_0(1-w_1),
\qquad
w_0(1-w_1)=\Gamma_Aw_1(1-w_0),
\]
together with their endpoints \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\).  The algorithm substitutes a rational parametrization of each arc, intersects it with every analytic sign stratum, and includes all resulting endpoints.  It also evaluates the two constant-\(U\) corners directly, where Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) gives \(q_a=r_a\).  When \(\Gamma_A=1\), subtraction of the two defining inequalities gives \(w_0=w_1\), so the algorithm instead optimizes on that diagonal.  These cases exhaust the topological boundary.

On the relative interior of every smooth branch, a local extremum either satisfies the two stationary equations or lies on a lower-dimensional branch face.  Implicit differentiation of \(F_a=0\) is legal because
\[
\frac{\partial F_a}{\partial z_a}
=\{1+(\vartheta-1)z_a\}
  \frac{d}{dz_a}\{(1-w_a)z_a+w_aT_\vartheta(z_a)\}>0,
\]
where positivity follows from the derivative calculation in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\).  Clearing the known positive denominators turns the stationary equations and the equations \(F_0=F_1=0\) into a finite polynomial system.  Saturation by the mixture denominators, arc denominators, Jacobian denominators, and branch-boundary polynomials removes precisely the components on which that clearing or that smooth-stratum derivation was illegal; those components have already been assigned to separate lower-dimensional strata.

For a zero-dimensional saturated system, successive resultants eliminate \(z_0,z_1\) and then one posterior coordinate.  Euclidean polynomial division terminates because degree strictly decreases.  The resulting univariate square-free factors have finitely many real roots.  Their signed-remainder sequences give exact rational isolating intervals: on an interval avoiding a remainder root, every sign is constant, and the difference in sign-variation counts at its endpoints equals the number of distinct roots; repeated bisection therefore isolates every root.  Back-substitution followed by rational interval Newton contraction certifies a unique solution box when the Jacobian is nonsingular.  Every box is then tested against the original, uncleared equations and inequalities, so a wrong quadratic branch or a zero-denominator artifact is rejected.

If a resultant vanishes identically, a Jacobian loses rank, roots collide, or the stationary ideal has positive dimension, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) does not use the generic resultant list.  It invokes sign-invariant cylindrical decomposition of the finite polynomial family consisting of the original constraints, all branch polynomials, and the objective comparison polynomials.  This procedure terminates by induction on the number of variables: in one variable the preceding signed-remainder isolation produces finitely many points and intervals; at each projection step only finitely many coefficients, discriminants, and pairwise resultants are added; over every cell of the lower-dimensional decomposition these projection polynomials have fixed signs, so finitely many isolated sections and sectors lift it to the next dimension.  On each lifted cell the original signs are invariant.  Hence root collisions and stationary continua are returned as exact algebraic cells rather than discarded.

Exhaustiveness now follows from compactness and finite stratification.  A minimum or maximum exists by Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\).  Its point is either in a zero-dimensional face, in the relative interior of a one-dimensional face where the tangential derivative vanishes, or in a two-dimensional smooth stratum where both derivatives vanish; if the relevant derivatives fail to define an isolated point, the cylindrical-decomposition case contains the entire singular or stationary component.  Thus every optimizer occurs on the enumerated list or cell.  Exact comparison of algebraic objective values is obtained by refining disjoint rational isolating intervals, or, at equality, by reducing their defining polynomials on the common algebraic cell.  Applying this finite procedure to \(H^-\) and \(H^+\) returns exact representations and membership certificates for \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  The construction uses the input as coefficients throughout and therefore proves only the stated fixed-input certificate, not a symbolic parameter atlas.
